transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-05 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Marta Gonzales (Synapse Head of AI), Evan Park (Synapse Platform Eng), Lisa Cho (Synapse PM)

Summary: Quick walkthrough of Redwood Console prompt-sets and Optimize; demo of regression alerts and A/B compare; touched on Dedicated vs Hosted, encryption/KMS and pilot next steps.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Priya, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Marta Gonzales: Good, thanks. Excited to see how you handle prompt-level regressions — we've had a couple of nasty surprises in production.
[00:12] Evan Park: Yep, time boxed, we have an hour, we also have a security checkpoint after this call.
[00:17] Priya Rao: Great, we'll try to keep things tight. Agenda first: show prompt sets in the Console, then Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization, then the regression alerts & A/B compare feature with a small live example.
[00:27] Lisa Cho: Sounds good. For context, our team runs a multi-turn recommendation assistant for checkout and post-purchase, so latency at tail matters and we have some privacy rules around customer IDs.
[00:38] Jordan Lee: Perfect, that's helpful. Marta, can you share the big win metric you want from this pilot?
[00:43] Marta Gonzales: Two things — reduce costly hallucinations in the top-10 recs, and keep 95th percentile latency under 350ms for inference. Cost is important but latency and quality first.
[00:55] Priya Rao: Noted. Quick note — when we talk about "Quality Beacon" in the demo that's just our internal shorthand for the prompt/regression product; it's the Eval & Monitoring page in the Console.
[01:04] Evan Park: I actually misheard you earlier, we thought you said "Quality Bison" in the invite, so the naming is fine.
[01:10] Jordan Lee: Cool. Ok Priya, can you share screen and show prompt sets?
[01:15] Priya Rao: Yep, sharing now. Give me one sec... All right, in the Console you'll see Prompt Sets on the left nav. We can create a set by uploading a CSV or connecting to your existing test harness. I'm going to demo by creating a small set called "checkout-happy-path-20" — these are 20 canonical prompts that represent cart flows.
[01:33] Marta Gonzales: Are those prompts tokenized or do you preserve the raw strings? We rely on raw strings for annotation.
[01:39] Priya Rao: We store both; the UI shows the raw prompt and the token profile. You can tag prompts as "critical" so alerts weight them higher.
[01:47] Evan Park: Is there an API for prompt sets? We need to integrate with our CI so new prompts are added automatically.
[01:53] Priya Rao: Yes, REST and SDK. We have an endpoint to push prompt batches and to fetch evaluation results.
[01:58] Lisa Cho: Good, we want to push new prompts from our nightly e2e tests.
[02:02] Priya Rao: Perfect. Moving to Optimize — this panel gives recommendations for batching, KV cache settings, and quantization profiles. For your workload, with short multi-turns, we often propose N=8 batching and int8 quantization on compatible models to shave cost without affecting top-N quality.
[02:19] Marta Gonzales: Have you seen int8 change hallucination rates?
[02:22] Priya Rao: In most models we onboard, we run a regression check — we compare on a control set and only recommend quantization if metrics are within an acceptable delta. That's surfaced here as a regression preview.
[02:33] Jordan Lee: To add, Optimize's suggestion will include both the expected token-cost reduction and an estimated quality delta. It doesn't blindly flip on quantization.
[02:42] Evan Park: Can we pin that to a canary rollout so we only expose 10% of traffic?
[02:46] Priya Rao: Absolutely. Our rollout controls let you do traffic splits between model variants and you can tie that to alert thresholds.
[02:53] Lisa Cho: Show the regression alerts please.
[02:55] Priya Rao: Switching to the Eval & Monitoring page. Here you can set a baseline: either a fixed historical baseline or a dynamic moving window. You set metrics like semantic-similarity, helpfulness, or custom classifiers. Alerts support webhooks, email, and PagerDuty.
[03:13] Jordan Lee: Note — our default suggestion for moving baselines is 7 days, but for retail bursts we recommend 24–72 hours to capture traffic swings.
[03:23] Marta Gonzales: Ok, how sensitive are the alerts? We had a previous system that flapped constantly.
[03:28] Priya Rao: You can set minimum effect sizes and require sustained drift across X samples before firing. Also we have "critical prompt" weighting so the top-10 prompts you mark will have lower thresholds.
[03:38] Evan Park: Any stats on false positives?
[03:41] Priya Rao: Our internal benchmarking shows about ~12% false-positive rate at default settings; we tune per-customer down to single digits by adjusting sample windows and thresholds. That's the tradeoff between detection speed and noise.
[03:52] Marta Gonzales: Love that. Now the A/B compare?
[03:54] Priya Rao: Right, A/B compare. I'll spin up a live compare between your current hosted model (we'll call it 'base') and a quantized candidate ('q8-candidate'). I have a 50-sample test prompt set ready.
[04:06] Lisa Cho: Is the statistical test a t-test or bootstrap?
[04:09] Priya Rao: We apply bootstrap confidence intervals for median metrics and a chi-squared for categorical pass/fail tests. The UI surfaces p-values and CIs and highlights where one arm beats the other.
[04:19] Jordan Lee: Quick caveat: the UI shows significance but we also recommend looking at lift by user segment and by prompt tags.
[04:27] Priya Rao: Running the compare now... (loading) ... ok results: mean semantic-similarity delta is -0.004 with 95% CI [-0.012, 0.004], p=0.18, so not significant. Latency 95th drops from 420ms to 320ms in the q8 arm.
[04:47] Marta Gonzales: That's promising for latency but I'd rather avoid any dip in top rec relevance.
[04:52] Priya Rao: Understood. We can do a weighted test emphasizing your top-10 critical prompts; re-running with weights... (brief pause) weighted delta on top-10 is +0.002 CI [-0.006, 0.010], p=0.34. So no significant hit.
[05:12] Evan Park: For the pilot, can we start with a 5% traffic split for 72 hours and then auto-increase to 20% if no alerts?
[05:20] Jordan Lee: Yes — our rollout policy templates include a step-up plan: 5% -> 20% -> 50% with hold windows and automatic rollback if regression alerts fire.
[05:30] Lisa Cho: On compliance, Marta had a question about KMS and logs.
[05:33] Marta Gonzales: Right — we need to ensure customer IDs are not persisted in Redwood logs and that keys are customer-managed.
[05:40] Jordan Lee: For Private and Dedicated, you can bring-your-own KMS and we don't store raw PII in search logs. We write audit logs to your S3 with masking options. For Hosted, we offer encrypted at rest with Redwood-managed keys but BYOK is available via an enterprise config.
[05:56] Evan Park: Do you support HSM-backed KMS?
[05:58] Priya Rao: Yes, HSM via partner KMS is supported in Private deployments.
[06:02] Marta Gonzales: Do you have SOC 2 Type II?
[06:05] Jordan Lee: Yes, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II certified; we can share the report under NDA.
[06:09] Lisa Cho: Great. Back to the demo — can you show how we tune alert thresholds?
[06:13] Priya Rao: Sure — in the alert creation modal you pick metric, baseline, min effect size, required consecutive windows, and which prompt tags apply. You can preview expected alert rate given the historical distribution.
[06:25] Jordan Lee: Important note: when you link alerts to rollouts, a firing alert can pause the rollout or trigger rollback — this is often how customers keep safety in automation.
[06:36] Marta Gonzales: I'm curious about model routing — we have bursty traffic during promotions, can Redwood route to cheaper models for low-priority queries?
[06:45] Priya Rao: Yes, smart routing can send low-priority routes to a lower-cost variant or a static cache; you define policies by route tag, latency SLO, or cost bucket.
[06:55] Evan Park: For the pilot we want: critical checkout prompts on Dedicated, other less sensitive paging on Hosted. Feels like a mixed deployment.
[07:03] Jordan Lee: That's a common pattern — Dedicated for SLO-critical flows, Hosted for lower-tier bulk workloads. We'll document the recommended routing policy for your traffic mix.
[07:11] Lisa Cho: Can you export the A/B results programmatically so our analytics pipeline can compute secondary metrics?
[07:16] Priya Rao: Yes — every experiment exposes a JSON results endpoint and a CSV export. You can plug that into your BI.
[07:22] Marta Gonzales: Any gotchas with session-level KV cache and multi-turn conversations?
[07:27] Priya Rao: Session KV cache helps latency but can increase memory. We recommend TTLs and a cache partitioning strategy for very large concurrent sessions. The Console's Optimize tab will suggest a KV TTL based on your session length distribution.
[07:38] Evan Park: How do we validate no-data-leak between tenants on Dedicated?
[07:42] Priya Rao: Dedicated is physically isolated GPU pools and we provide tenant isolation at the runtime level; we also surface audit logs and periodic verification scripts.
[07:52] Jordan Lee: Ok, quick live example — Priya will show alert configuration for the "checkout-happy-path-20" set.
[07:58] Priya Rao: Creating alert... metric: semantic-similarity (BERT-sim), baseline: 14-day rolling, min effect: 0.01, consecutive windows: 3, severity: high for critical-tagged prompts. You can add webhook to your Slack channel.
[08:18] Lisa Cho: Is there an alert cooldown window? We don't want repeated spam.
[08:21] Priya Rao: Yes a cooldown and backoff. Defaults to 1h but configurable.
[08:26] Marta Gonzales: This looks solid. For the pilot dataset, we'll send the top-20 prompts and a 1-week historical sample of traffic.
[08:34] Jordan Lee: Great — we'll prepare the pilot run plan and a dashboard template for the first 72 hours.
[08:40] Evan Park: Security-wise, we'll send the security checklist and our infosec will request a short call — can you join if needed?
[08:46] Jordan Lee: Absolutely. We usually loop in our security lead and the infra SE, happy to do a focused review.
[08:52] Lisa Cho: One last question — can we set a post-deploy smoke test that runs a small set of golden prompts through the canary before enabling traffic step-up?
[08:59] Priya Rao: Yes, deployment playbooks can include a pre-step smoke test that gates the rollout if metrics degrade.
[09:06] Marta Gonzales: Ok final ask: we'd like recommendations on prompt engineering — like templating, few-shot choices and safety filters. Do you provide that?
[09:14] Priya Rao: We offer a prompt-engineering playbook and an optional workshop with our solutions team; we can include that in the pilot scope.
[09:22] Jordan Lee: Recap & next steps: Synapse to share prompt corpus and policy, Redwood to send pilot pricing and SLA, Redwood SE to provide batching/quantization config and run a quick bakeoff.
[09:34] Marta Gonzales: Thanks, Jordan, Priya. Expect the corpus by next Wednesday.
[09:38] Evan Park: We'll also open a ticket with our security questions.
[09:41] Jordan Lee: Great. We'll target pilot kickoff week of 2026-06-15. Thanks everyone.
[09:46] Lisa Cho: Thanks all.
